searches.purpose: Locate Vygotsky primary and edition records, independent post-Vygotskian historiography, theory and double-stimulation method sources, a bounded contemporary empirical re-use, present institutional continuation and Russian-to-English/Portuguese translation analysis while keeping Vygotsky's cultural-historical theory distinct from later Leontiev/Engeström activity theory, broad sociocultural learning theory, scaffolding, social constructivism and generic culturally informed psychology

items.title: Rethinking the Early History of Post-Vygotskian Psychology: The Case of the Kharkov School
items.rights_note: Official Europe PMC bibliographic and abstract record for independent historiography of the post-1934 Kharkov school; the abstract does not establish the full argument, and the Kharkov line is not treated as identical to Vygotsky's own programme.
items.failure_note: The PubMed landing page presented a reCAPTCHA shell to automated access on 2026-07-30; the official Europe PMC core record endpoint was selected without attempting to solve or bypass the challenge. A candidate Springer DOI was rejected after the Europe PMC record identified the correct APA DOI.

items.title: Thought and Language
items.rights_note: Open Library record for the 1962 MIT Press English edition translated from Myshlenie i rech; preview access does not authorize caching or treating the copyrighted book body as read, and later sources document abridgement and translation problems.

items.title: History of the Development of Higher Mental Functions
items.rights_note: CC BY-NC 4.0 Russian journal reprint of a Vygotsky text on the cultural development of higher mental functions; the 1996 publication date is a reprint date, not the date of original composition. The PDF is visually readable but uses a legacy Cyrillic encoding that produces mojibake in automated extraction, and the machine-linked English translation is not treated as an authoritative edition.

items.title: 100 Years of the Development of Cultural-Historical Psychology: Milestones and Directions
items.rights_note: CC BY-NC 4.0 centennial overview by senior participants maps signs, higher psychological functions, personality, cooperation and double stimulation; it is an internal synthetic account and not independent validation of the school.

items.title: Revisionist Revolution in Vygotsky Studies: The State of the Art
items.rights_note: Publisher description and contents for a revisionist edited volume addressing chronology, authorship, archives, suppression narratives and translation; the copyrighted chapters are not cached or treated as read, and later critics contest parts of this revisionist programme.

items.title: The Revisionist Revolution and Future Prospects of Vygotskian Studies
items.rights_note: CC BY-NC 4.0 critical response challenges elements of Yasnitsky's revisionist project and its proposed cultural-historical Gestalt psychology; retaining both sides records a live historiographical dispute rather than selecting one camp as settled fact.

items.title: Intellectual Development of Elementary Schoolchildren and Their Performance on the Vygotsky-Sakharov Method
items.rights_note: CC BY-NC 4.0 study of 197 Moscow first- and third-grade pupils that attempts to reproduce the Vygotsky-Sakharov double-stimulation task and reports partial correspondence; this tests one method and sample, not cultural-historical psychology as a unified theory.

items.title: Works of Vygotsky and His Translations: Discussing Some Concepts
items.rights_note: CC BY-NC 4.0 comparison of Russian editions and Brazilian Portuguese translations documents omissions, added material and contested renderings such as zona blizhaishego razvitiia; its proposed translation is an argued choice, not a universal terminological settlement.

items.title: Cultural-Historical Psychology: Journal About and Scope
items.rights_note: Current Moscow State University of Psychology and Education journal self-description records quarterly Russian/English publication, open access and ISCAR affiliation; it demonstrates an active publication venue, not agreement across variants or empirical validity.
